sentences.text: The name Jucha reflects a key feature: the holotype fossil lacks a skull.
This specimen is encased in a mineral crust of mainly pyrite, which is why the specific epithet is squalea.
The genus name honors a figure from Turkic demonology known for having snake skin and the ability to remove her head.
Fully grown individuals of this animal reached a length of approximately 5 meters.
The holotype specimen was discovered in 2007 near the village of Slantsevy Rudnik in European Russia.
The genus and species Jucha squalea were formally described in 2020 by Fisher and colleagues.
Jucha is an extinct genus of plesiosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
The type species Jucha squalea is considered one of the most basal and oldest known definitive elasmosaurs.
Jucha lived during the Hauterivian stage, between 132.6 and 125.77 million years ago.
